page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel Xeon 6448H processor containing 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with shared allocation, featuring 16 MB of L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 180.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.25 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM inference tasks. For a small 135M model, it achieves a prompt processing speed of 13,631.52 tokens per second and a text generation speed of 610.8 tokens per second. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing reaches 6,293.73 tokens per second with a text generation speed of 153.1 tokens per second. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier, registering 35.53 GB/sec and 15.59 GB/sec respectively. General CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, fall within the average tier.

The server offers a high-density resource profile, combining a professional-grade accelerator with substantial system memory and NVMe storage. The shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, non-shared CPU performance, though the physical core count and hardware-assisted instruction sets help mitigate processing bottlenecks. This configuration is highly cost-efficient for GPU-accelerated workloads that do not require dedicated CPU pinning. It is primarily suited for large language model inference, machine learning workloads, data science tasks, and memory-intensive database operations.
